extracted.intended_audience: Catholic children, catechism students, and parishioners preparing for sacraments (esp. Matrimony) and devotional practices
extracted.subtask_description: Question-and-answer catechetical guidance on the Sacrament of Matrimony and on sacramentals (Sign of the Cross, holy water, rosary, scapulars, etc.), including requirements for valid/worthy reception, preparatory duties, and correct devotional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Sacrament of Matrimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sacrament of Matrimony is the Sacrament which unites a Christian man and woman in lawful marriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 'Christian' persons receive the grace of the Sacrament; marriage raised by Christ to the dignity of a Sacrament (distinguishing it from mere contractual unions before Christ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful Christian marriage requires the Sacrament
rubrics_metrics.description: A Christian man and woman cannot be united in lawful marriage in any other way than by the Sacrament of Matrimony, because Christ raised marriage to the dignity of a Sacrament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that civil or other ceremonies do not confer the sacramental grace of Matrimony for Christians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage must comply with laws of God and of the Church (lawful)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons are lawfully married when they comply with all the laws of God and of the Church relating to marriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To marry unlawfully is a mortal sin; persons should ensure compliance before proceeding. Examples of laws include prohibitions on certain times (Advent, Lent), consanguinity, mixed religion, age, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indissolubility of the marriage bond
rubrics_metrics.description: The bond of Christian marriage cannot be dissolved by any human power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Church may permit separation for good reason, spouses remain married; when the Church declares a marriage null it is because an impediment made it invalid from the beginning, not because the Church dissolved a valid bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impediments to marriage and duty to disclose them
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons planning marriage must tell the priest every circumstance that might be an impediment to the marriage (these circumstances may render the marriage null or unlawful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief items to disclose (privately if possible): whether both are Christians/Catholics; prior solemn engagements; vows to God (chastity/religious life); degree of relationship; prior marriages within the other's family; godparent relationships with each other or children; prior marriage and proof of death of former spouse; true intention to marry; lawful age; health or sickness that might prevent marriage; parish residence and duration. Give at least three weeks' notice before marriage except in special necessity. Do not invite or finalize arrangements before consulting the pastor to avoid inconvenience if impediments are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church authority over marriage laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church alone has the right to make laws concerning the Sacrament of marriage, though the State also has the right to make laws concerning the civil effects of the marriage contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil effects include property, inheritance, and debts; ecclesiastical law governs sacramental validity and observance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbidden mixed marriages (Catholic with non-Catholic or no religion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church does forbid the marriage of Catholics with persons who have a different religion or no religion at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning: such marriages generally lead to indifference, loss of faith, neglect of children's religious education, domestic conflict over religion, and exposure of the Catholic party to bad example and spiritual danger. The Church also discourages insincere conversions for the sake of marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worthy motives for marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons should enter marriage with worthy motives: to fulfill the end for which God instituted marriage, not solely for money, property, or worldly advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worthy motives are discerned by serious consideration and by valuing the desire to please God and lead a good life; every person's motive should be to serve God better in that state than in any other.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Christians should prepare for marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: Christians should prepare for a holy and happy marriage by receiving the Sacraments of Penance and Holy Eucharist; by begging God to grant a pure intention and to direct their choice; and by seeking the advice of their parents and the blessing of their pastors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should pray long, read Scripture examples (e.g., Tobias and Sara), ask prudent persons about the other's former life and family, consult a confessor if parents are unreasonable, and ensure a well-considered, informed choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of the Sacrament of Matrimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The effects are: first, to sanctify the love of husband and wife; second, to give them grace to bear with each other's weaknesses; third, to enable them to bring up their children in the fear and love of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents receive special grace to advise, direct, and warn children of sin; failure to use this grace is gravely culpable.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of grace and compliance required to receive Matrimony worthily
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the Sacrament of Matrimony worthily it is necessary to be in the state of grace, and it is necessary also to comply with the laws of the Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References include laws forbidding solemnizing marriage at certain times (Advent and Lent), prohibitions concerning relatives, mixed religion, and requirements of age and other canonical conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and function of sacramentals
rubrics_metrics.description: A sacramental is anything set apart or blessed by the Church to excite good thoughts and to increase devotion, and through these movements of the heart to remit venial sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not the sacramental itself that gives grace, but the devotion, love of God, or sorrow for sin that it inspires; the more devotion in using sacramentals, the more grace one may obtain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between Sacraments and sacramentals
rubrics_metrics.description: First, the Sacraments were instituted by Jesus Christ and the sacramentals were instituted by the Church; second, the Sacraments give grace of themselves when we place no obstacle in the way; the sacramentals excite in us pious dispositions, by means of which we may obtain grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Church can increase or diminish the number of sacramentals, but not the number of Sacraments.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sign of the Cross as chief sacramental and its correct form
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief sacramental used in the Church is the Sign of the Cross. We make it by putting the right hand to the forehead, then on the breast, and then to the left and right shoulders; saying, 'In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is important to make an exact cross and to say all the words distinctly. Anti-patterns: merely touching forehead and breast, forehead and chin, or failing to touch are not the true Sign of the Cross—these are only signs or movements and not the full sacramental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning expressed by the Sign of the Cross
rubrics_metrics.description: We make the Sign of the Cross to show that we are Christians and to profess our belief in the chief mysteries of our religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: 'In the name' expresses the Unity of God; 'of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost' expresses the Trinity; the gesture also recalls the Incarnation and death of Our Lord and other theological truths (original sin, Christ's love and sacrifice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holy water: definition and intended effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Holy water is water blessed by the priest with solemn prayer to beg God's blessing on those who use it, and protection from the power of darkness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the priest prays that those who use it may not fall into sin and may be free from the devil and bodily diseases, those who use the water receive the benefit of those prayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other sacramentals and their meanings (candles, ashes, palms, crucifix, images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides the Sign of the Cross and holy water there are many sacramentals, such as blessed candles, ashes, palms, crucifixes, images of the Blessed Virgin and of the saints, rosaries, and scapulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: candles (wax from flowers→Christ's human body; flame→divinity; lights as sign of joy and honor), ashes on Ash Wednesday as sign of penance, palms for Christ's triumph into Jerusalem, crucifix (has image of Our Lord) vs cross (no figure), images as statues/pictures to recall holy persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rosary structure and devotional practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The rosary (beads) contains fifty-three small beads for 'Hail Marys' and six large beads for 'Our Fathers'; the Rosary as used includes fifteen Mysteries (five Joyful, five Sorrowful, five Glorious) on which one meditates before each decade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In saying the Rosary one stops after mentioning the Mystery to meditate on the lesson it teaches before saying the 'Our Father' and 'Hail Marys'. Generally the beads cover one third of the Rosary (five mysteries); to say the whole Rosary one must go over them three times. If said every day, the whole Rosary is said twice a week and one day is spare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and seasonal rules for saying the Rosary mysteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Mysteries are assigned by day and season: Monday—Joyful; Tuesday—Sorrowful; Wednesday—Glorious; Thursday—Joyful; Friday—Sorrowful; Saturday—Glorious. On Sundays (except Sundays of Advent and Lent) always say the Glorious Mysteries. In Advent say the Joyful, in Lent the Sorrowful; in Eastertime always the Glorious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mysteries run in the order of events in Our Lord's life; the practice helps regular meditation aligned with liturgical seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.N.R.I. and I.H.S. abbreviations explained
rubrics_metrics.description: I.N.R.I. are the first letters of four Latin words meaning 'Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.' I.H.S. (with a cross) is an abbreviation for 'Jesus' as first written in Greek letters or taken for the Latin words meaning 'Jesus, Saviour of men.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inscriptions often appear on altars and holy things and carry theological signification (e.g., I.H.S. with a cross can signify that He saved men by His death on the Cross).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scapular: description, purpose, and devotional meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The scapular (small two-piece version worn under garments) is worn to indicate that one places oneself under the special protection of the Blessed Virgin; it is a mark of special devotion to Mary and originated with the Carmelite Fathers (Scapular of Mount Carmel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different colors honor different devotions (brown—Mount Carmel; red—for Our Lord's Passion; white—for the Holy Trinity; blue—for the Immaculate Conception; black—for the seven dolors). The Church grants privileges and indulgences to those who wear the scapular. It is a 'uniform' signifying special service to the Blessed Virgin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holy Oils and sacraments using oil
rubrics_metrics.description: Three kinds of oil blessed by the bishop on Holy Thursday: oil of the infirm (for the sick), oil of catechumens (used in Baptism and priestly ordination), and holy chrism (used in Baptism, Confirmation, and when the bishop blesses sacred vessels and altars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sacraments in which oil is used: Baptism (two kinds used), Confirmation, Extreme Unction (Anointing of the Sick), and Holy Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of youth to learn religion and respect teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Children should learn their religion while young, attend Sunday/day school, and respect and not distract teachers; learning religious instruction prepares one to answer about the faith and profit from later instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglecting religious lessons leads to spiritual misery in this world and the next; parents' example and teachers' sacrifices should be appreciated. Practical admonition: do not waste time in school, study diligently, and value religious instruction as a unique opportunity.
